facts.claim: Cambridge Dictionary defines a maid of honour as the most important bridesmaid at a marriage ceremony (US spelling: maid of honor).
facts.quote: the most important bridesmaid at a marriage ceremony

facts.claim: Cambridge Dictionary defines a matron of honour as, at a wedding, a married woman who helps the woman who is getting married; its usage example has the groom's speech thanking the bridesmaids and matron of honour.
facts.quote: at a wedding (= a ceremony at which two people get married), a married woman who helps the woman who is getting married : The groom ended his speech by thanking the bridesmaids and matron of honour.

facts.claim: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary defines a bridesmaid as a young woman or girl who helps a bride before and during the marriage ceremony; the word dates from the late 18th century as an alteration of the earlier 'bridemaid'.
facts.quote: a young woman or girl who helps a bride before and during the marriage ceremony ... Word Origin late 18th cent.: alteration of earlier bridemaid.
facts.conflicts: Word-origin line may overlap batch A (history); batch B uses only the 'before and during' role definition.

facts.claim: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary defines maid of honour as (especially in the US) a young woman or girl who is the main bridesmaid at a wedding, and points readers to compare matron of honour.
facts.quote: (especially in the US) a young woman or girl who is the main bridesmaid at a wedding compare matron of honour
facts.conflicts: Consistent with Cambridge (fact_100): both describe the maid of honour as the chief or most important bridesmaid. Oxford adds 'especially in the US'.

facts.claim: Cambridge Dictionary defines a groomsman (mainly US; UK usually 'usher') as a friend of a man who is getting married who has special duties at the wedding, including showing people to their seats.
facts.quote: a friend of a man who is getting married who has special duties at the wedding including showing people to their seats
facts.conflicts: No Cambridge or Oxford Learner's entry for 'bridesman' was read; bridesman is written as living practice.

insider_details.detail: Both Cambridge and Oxford treat the maid of honour as the chief bridesmaid and the matron of honour as the married equivalent, so the lead attendant's title can simply follow the couple's preference; the role itself is the same lead-helper job.

The core definition of a bridesmaid is someone who helps the bride before and during the ceremony, which is the frame for the roles section: helping with plans in the months before, then getting ready, the bouquet and the processional on the day.
Seating guests is a defined groomsman (UK: usher) duty; in a mixed party, bridesmen and groomswomen can share those on-the-day jobs, which is living practice rather than dictionary usage.

When inviting attendants to travel, ask early enough for each person to check their passport has at least six months' validity beyond the trip and to arrange their own travel insurance that covers every country on the route, including stopovers, and cancellation if plans change.
Share one wedding-week itinerary with the whole party and suggest they keep hard copies of flights, accommodation and event bookings; attendants declare any health conditions to their own insurer.
